subject: MedStack packaging questions and pilot SOW
messages:
From: Holly Jennings <holly@medstack.com>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Packaging question — usage and a possible tier swap

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We ran the team-level usage export for October and attached our top-line numbers (MedStack_usage_oct.csv). We're evaluating whether to move from Compact to a throughput-oriented plan for Q1 — primarily because our nightly batch inference and API peak windows are growing.

Two quick questions to help us model cost and impact:
- If we upgrade to the Throughput tier, which premium features are bundled vs available as add-ons? Specifically: per-request KV cache persistence and priority routing.
- Do you have a short SOW template for a pilot (1 mo) that includes a committed burst and a rollback timeline? We're sensitive to costs and want to cap exposure if throughput ramps unexpectedly.

If helpful, I'll bring our engineering lead (cc: sales_ops@medstack.com) into a follow-up. We aim to decide by end of month.

Cheers,
Holly Jennings
Head of Data Platform
MedStack

Attachment: MedStack_usage_oct.csv (csv)

From: naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Holly Jennings <holly@medstack.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Packaging question — usage and a possible tier swap

Hi Holly — thanks for the export and the clear asks. I pulled a quick summary and jotted a few initial playbook notes (attached).

Short answers up front:
- Throughput tier bundles: steady-state priority routing, autoscaling to a committed qps, and a base KV-cache policy. Per-request persistent KV cache is an add-on we typically include during a pilot if the workload benefits (e.g., many repeated prompts).
- We do have a simple pilot SOW we use for burst + rollback; I attached a draft SOW template (MedStack_SOW_draft_v1.docx) and my notes.

Couple of clarifying Qs to size the right packaging:
1) What is your expected 95th percentile qps in peak windows? (ballpark ok)
2) How latency-sensitive are interactive requests vs batch jobs? If interactive is <200ms SLO, we should prioritize lower-latency instance types.
3) Do you need obligations around data residency / audit logs for the pilot?

I'll loop Ben for pricing scenarios and Karthik for a technical pilot configuration after you confirm the three bullets.

—Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0182

Attachment: playbook_notes_naomi.txt (text)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Holly Jennings <holly@medstack.com>, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 16 Nov 2027 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Pricing options for MedStack pilot (3 scenarios)

Hi Holly — looping in a few pricing scenarios to illustrate tradeoffs. Naomi, feel free to edit.

Summary (three short options):
1) Small pilot (risk-min): 4-week pilot, reserved burst up to 2x current peak, no long-term commit. Price: $8k flat pilot fee + $0.012/token for generation overage. Add-on: per-request KV persistence available at $1k/mo opt-in.
2) Pilot-to-commit (discount path): 8-week pilot with option to convert to a 12-month partial commit. Pilot discounted fee $12k includes 20% credit toward first 3 months if converted. During conversion, Throughput tier bundle applies (includes priority routing, base KV cache).
3) Throughput commit (best unit cost): 12-month commit with stepped discounts at 12/24/36 months; starts with an initial credit for onboarding. Price varies by committed qps; I can send a modeled spreadsheet if you share 95th percentile qps.

We can cap month-over-month spend during the pilot with a soft limit and an automatic rollback to Compact if consumption exceeds the agreed threshold — we do that with a short amendment in the SOW. I've attached a simple spreadsheet with modeled examples (pricing_options_3up.xlsx).

Next steps we suggest:
- Holly: confirm the three technical bullets Naomi asked so Karthik can propose instance sizing and KV cache toggles.
- If you want, we can draft the pilot SOW and include a hard cap clause for approval.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachment: pricing_options_3up.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Holly Jennings <holly@medstack.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 21 Nov 2027 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pricing options for MedStack pilot (3 scenarios)

Thanks Ben and Naomi — this is helpful. A couple of follow-ups from our PM and finance team after reviewing the options: 

- For the pilot we want the per-request KV persistence included (we have a lot of repeated prompt patterns) but we also want clarity on which features become "bundled" vs "add-on" if we convert to Throughput. Can you provide a one-line matrix that maps features -> included in Throughput | add-on | enterprise only?
- Finance asked if the pilot can include a hard cap on total spend (not just a soft limit). If consumption exceeds the cap we agree we revert to Compact and send an overage invoice after a reconciliation period.
- Also request a lightweight SOW that shows the rollback timeline (48h to enact rollback after trigger), pilot start/end dates, and acceptance criteria (api p95 latency < 250ms for interactive, successful KV hit-rate > 60% for the chosen dataset).

If you can send the matrix and a revised SOW with the cap clause I can get internal approval quickly. Appreciate keeping the SOW short — we prefer a one-page pilot annex.

Best,
Holly
Head of Data Platform, MedStack
